> Always have a manual way to control a device if HA goes down.

It is for this reason that my lights (Hue) and switches (Inovelli) are bound in ZigBee groups. HA adds some niceties, but the lights still work if it’s down. Accent lights I have bound to the Hue Bridge, because their app adds features HA doesn’t have, and they aren’t required for emergency egress.

The only gap I have, I think, is that because I’ve set all bulbs to respond to power restoration after a cut in last known state, if everything somehow lost its Zigbee binding, putting switches into dumb mode locally still wouldn’t help. However, since that’s an improbable scenario, I accept the remote possibility in exchange for not being awakened from lights coming on in the middle of the night. Plus I keep flashlights / headlamps throughout the house.

No, the question asked was whether binaries output by scriptc, such as the tsc-ts compiler binary, include a garbage collector that runs while they're running. (The question was not about the output of tsc-ts.) If not, then that would raise a bunch of questions about how the TypeScript code that was fed into scriptc is being executed without a GC. It is true that a TypeScript compiler could be written in a non-GC language like Rust, but tsc-ts in particular is written in TypeScript, which needs a GC.

The answer, according to https://scriptc.dev/docs/limitations#weak-collections-and-me..., is that scriptc relies primarily on reference counting, augmented with a cycle collector that runs at specific times, kind of like Python.
